newsitem.title: USA: Dow to boost chlorine, caustic soda output.
newsitem.headline: Dow to boost chlorine, caustic soda output.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Monday it planned to increase its North American and European capacity to produce chlorine and caustic soda by 420,000 metric tonnes to about 6.2 million metric tonnes.
The increase, which equals about one percent of total worldwide capacity, is in response to stronger demand, the chemical company said in a press release.
Dow Chemical is the largest producer of chlorine and caustic soda with about 13 percent of global capacity in 1996.

A new membrane evaporator at Dow Chemical's Stade, Germany, chlorine and caustic stoda facility is expected to start by the end of the third quarter of 1998. In the 1998 fourth quarter, 120,000 metric tonnes of chlorine capacity will be added to the site's capacity.
In the second quarter of 1999, Dow Chemical said it would increase chlorine capacity at a Freeport, Texas, plant by 300,000 metric tonnes.
Brian Ames, global caustic-soda marketing manager, said the market for chlorine and caustic soda was growing at 1.5 percent to 2.5 percent annually.
